helpCenter.multiDevice.headline: Multi-device: every device is a Bakabase server
helpCenter.multiDevice.intro: Every device can run its own Bakabase: the all-in-one desktop app on a computer, or the server on a NAS or another host. Each manages its own storage and resources. You decide which devices may browse or manage it. Both desktop apps and headless servers can manage other devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.title: Three Bakabase servers on one local network, each with its own storage
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.d: Its movies stay on its own drive. Once management is allowed, Resources → All devices can show and manage resources on the other devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.l: Keeps the comics on its own disk. It can do everything the desktop PC can: every computer is an equal, not a client of another.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.n: Its music stays here. Open its address in a browser to manage it. It can also add and manage other devices without a desktop window.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.hint: Select a device to highlight its connections.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.title: What every device has
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.server.des: The desktop app includes a complete Bakabase server; a NAS runs the same server in Docker.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.storage.de: Each device keeps its own disks and its own library. Resources and their values are never copied between devices; only the definitions you choose to sync are kept the same.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.reach.desc: Desktop apps and servers can both browse libraries shared with them and manage devices that allow them to do so.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.title: Two ways to use another device
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.title: Multi-device library
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.desc: Search and view libraries shared with this device. Read-only sharing allows browsing and compatible media playback without changing the source data.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.title: Unified management
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.desc: View managed resources, properties and media libraries together. Changes are saved on their owning device, without first switching the entire window.
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.title: Side by side
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.brows: Resources from all devices, merged, in this computer's interface
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.switc: Managed resources grouped by their source device, using this device’s interface
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.browse: Search, view details, preview and play; nothing changes on the other device
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.switch: Edit resource properties and library memberships; manage custom property and library definitions. Device settings remain on that device’s own page.
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.brow: On the computer you sit at
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.swit: In the browser or the viewing device’s desktop app, depending on file access and player capabilities
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.br: Library sharing: a share code, or being allowed — browse only
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.sw: Management: a pairing code, or being allowed — full control
helpCenter.multiDevice.trust: Nothing connects on its own. Each device decides who may browse its library and who may manage it, and can take that back at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.title: See how your devices connect
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.desc: The Device map (left menu → Multi-device → Device map) draws this computer in the middle and your other devices around it, with a line for every connection: library sharing, and who manages whom. Select a device or a line to see its details and act on it — allow, revoke, switch to it, map its folders. Devices found nearby appear as outlines you can add. Data sync lines show which device receives another's definitions.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.headline: Every device's library in one window
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.intro: Multi-device library searches this computer and the devices that share with it, and merges the results into one list. Each device still answers for its own resources; nothing is copied here.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.mock.capti: “This device” shows only what is on the computer you sit at.
“All devices” adds the laptop's comics and the NAS's music to the same list, each marked with the device it lives on.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.searc: Match names and file names across the devices you choose. Advanced property filters stay in each device's own library.
Details are read-only. Previews and the player run on this computer and nothing is written back, not even play history. Opening a folder needs a path mapping.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.cover: A device that is offline is reported as not searched, never silently left out of results that look complete.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.boundary: Read-only sharing does not allow changes. Establish a management connection, then open Resources → All devices to edit data. Device-level actions remain on the owning device’s management page.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.headline: Manage several devices in one place
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.intro: Desktop apps and headless servers can both be managers. After adding a device, Resources → All devices groups resources by source and provides custom property and media library management. Changes stay on their owner; missing file mappings or playback capabilities do not block metadata editing. The window switcher below is an additional desktop feature for opening another device’s full interface.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.local: This computer's own library, settings and tasks.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.remot: {{name}}'s library, settings and tasks. Changes made here happen on {{name}}.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.capti: The window shows this computer. Pick another device in the list to switch to it.
The window shows {{name}}, and the switcher turns amber to say so. Pick this device at the top of the list to come back.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.title: Managing data and playing files are separate capabilities
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.capti: The viewing device keeps separate path mappings for each source. Local apps can open mapped files, while browsers and compatible players can use media streams from the source. Headless servers do not launch desktop players.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.ownUi: The window shows the interface that device ships with, so it always matches the version it runs.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.contr: Management permits changes to the other device’s data and settings. Only allow devices you trust. If A manages B, B does not automatically see A’s resources, and A does not inherit access to devices managed by B.
If a device runs an older version whose interface has no switcher, use “Switch to” in the tray icon's menu to come back.
Asks the device to revoke this computer, then deletes its key here. The device can also revoke this computer at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.headline: Set it up on the Devices and sharing page
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.intro: Both desktop apps and servers have Devices and sharing under Multi-device. Open a server’s address in a browser to configure it. Access is granted on the device being accessed, separately for each pair.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.shar: Turn on sharing on the other device
On its Devices and sharing page, under Library sharing, choose Turn on sharing. It shows its address there and can create a share code.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.conn: Under Library sharing → Add a device to browse, find nearby devices or enter its address. Enter its share code, or choose Ask to browse and allow it on the other device.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.both: Keep “Also let it browse this device's library” ticked (the default), and each device can browse the other once it's allowed.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.enab: The Multi-device library turns on by itself once you can browse a device. Open it and search all devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.allo: Allow it on the device to be managed
On its Devices and sharing page, under Management → Who may manage this device, turn on remote access (paired devices only). You can create a pairing code there too.
Add it on the managing device

Under Devices and sharing → Management → Add a device to manage, enter its address and pairing code. Without a code, request management and allow it on the other device. Desktop apps and headless servers both support this.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.swit: Open Resources → All devices to view and manage resources, properties and media libraries. Desktop apps can additionally use Open in this window for the other device’s settings.
To open files with a local app, add a path mapping for that source on the viewing device. Managing metadata or browsing compatible media does not require a mapping.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.unrestricte: Docker servers default to Unrestricted, allowing network devices to access them without pairing. Bakabase shows a reminder. To change access, open the server’s address and adjust Configuration → Remote access.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.nas: Headless servers also provide Devices and sharing: they can share libraries, manage other devices and receive management requests. Open their address in a browser. Environment variables and the federation CLI remain available for configuration.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.codes: Share codes and pairing codes are different: a share code only lets a device browse your library; a pairing code gives it full control. Share codes belong to Library sharing, pairing codes to Management.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.s: Letting other devices browse your library — view only, never change.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.l:
A device shares its library only once sharing is on there, and only with devices you allow: added with a share code from it, or by allowing a request in its notifications or under Devices and sharing → Library sharing.
Sharing has a direction. Browsing the NAS doesn't let the NAS browse you, and it never passes on to a third device. “Also let it browse this device's library”, ticked by default when you add a device, sets up the way back in the same step, so one approval covers both directions.
Sharing is view-only: the other device can search, view and play, but can't edit or delete anything.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.e:
On the laptop: Devices and sharing → Library sharing → Turn on sharing → Create share code.
On the desktop PC: Library sharing → Add a device to browse → the laptop's address and share code, with “Also let it browse this device's library” ticked → Add with share code.
Both can now browse each other in the Multi-device library.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.managemen: Full control of another device, granted on that device.

Management and sharing are separate permissions. Both desktop apps and headless servers can manage devices. Under Resources → All devices, edit resource properties, library membership, and property and library definitions; changes are saved on the owning device. Device-wide settings remain on that device’s own page.
The managed device grants permission: enable remote access under Devices and sharing → Management → Who may manage this device, then create a pairing code and enter it on the managing device. Alternatively, choose Ask to manage on the managing device and approve the request on the other device.
Management is one-way and grants no reverse or indirect access. Stop managing requests revocation and deletes the local key; the managed device can also revoke access at any time under Who may manage this device.
Allowing a request shows the requesting device's name and address. Make sure it is the computer you expect before you allow it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.pathMappi: Where another device's folders are, seen from the computer you sit at.

A path mapping describes where the same files are accessible on the viewing device, usually through a network share mounted beforehand. Each source has its own mappings. They are used locally and never copy or move files.
The desktop app can use local resource profiles to open mapped files with local players or default applications. Without a mapping, browsers and compatible remote-capable players can still use the source’s media streams. Games and other files that cannot be streamed need locally accessible files.
Viewing and editing resource metadata does not require path mappings.

The NAS keeps its music under /volume1/music, and this PC reaches the same folder as \\nas\music. With the mapping /volume1/music → \\nas\music, playing /volume1/music/Live/01.flac opens \\nas\music\Live\01.flac in this PC's player.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.remoteAcc: Which other devices a server answers, and what they may do.

Each Bakabase server has remote access settings controlling access from other devices. Management connections and read-only library sharing use separate permissions.
Docker defaults to Unrestricted. To change this, open that device’s address and adjust Access from other devices under Configuration → Remote access. Desktop apps may also use Open in this window. Bakabase never changes another device’s access settings on its own.
Only use Unrestricted on a network where you trust every device: anyone who can reach it can delete files and change settings. Never expose Bakabase to the internet with port forwarding.
